beats.idea: Character-level modeling maps characters to ints instead of GPT-2 BPE tokens, so the script first needs the whole corpus as text.
beats.shows: The learner can say in one sentence what the script produces and why getting text comes first.

beats.idea: The download is guarded: the path is built next to the script, and the file is fetched only if it does not already exist, so it happens once.
beats.shows: The learner can point at the existence check on line 14 and predict that a second run skips the request.

beats.idea: The file is then opened and read in full into a single string, with no splitting by line or word.
beats.shows: The learner can point at the read call on line 20 and see the result is one long string whose length counts characters.

beats.idea: The recorded run says the string is 1,115,394 characters; every later count works from that number.
beats.shows: The learner can check that 1,003,854 + 111,540 = 1,115,394, previewing that the later split loses nothing.

brief.to: Now that the text sits in one string, the next step is finding which distinct characters it contains.
